facts: A one-click verdict on a single assistant message.

A rated submission is the one case where `text` may be empty: the whole point of a thumb is that it costs nothing, and demanding prose to record it would collect the opinions of the patient and no one else.
The category a thumb stands for, so every surface agrees on the mapping.
Deliberately NOT `.min(1)` and deliberately NOT capped.

Not `.min(1)`, because a thumbs-up carries no prose and refusing it would throw away the cheapest signal we have; the `rating` refinement below is what keeps an empty body from being a legal ordinary submission.

Not capped, because the only consumer that cares about length — the feedback-hub envelope — TRUNCATES (`BODY_MAX_CODEPOINTS`). A ceiling here would turn a pasted 30k-character log into a 400, which loses the report instead of the tail of it.

ai.title: Cap follow-up suggestion tool calls per response and cancel the step request
ai.summary: A runaway model that repeats a follow-up suggestion tool (`suggest_prompts`, `suggest_followups`) inside one response now hits a cap of 8 calls per response, defined by `MAX_FOLLOWUP_SUGGESTION_CALLS_PER_RESPONSE` in stream-parser.ts, after which the tool stops being executed and the streaming consumption loop stops reading. Once the cap is exceeded, `processStream` invokes the `stopStream` callback (wired in run-agent-step.ts as a per-step AbortController abort), which cancels only this step's model request without cancelling the run, so tool completion and history finalization proceed normally. A system-tagged message carrying `FOLLOWUP_SUGGESTION_LIMIT_MESSAGE` is appended with tag `FOLLOWUP_SUGGESTION_LIMIT` so the turn ends cleanly rather than forcing another step.
ai.evidence: packages/agent-runtime/src/tools/stream-parser.ts adds `MAX_FOLLOWUP_SUGGESTION_CALLS_PER_RESPONSE = 8` and `FOLLOWUP_SUGGESTION_TOOL_NAMES` (a set of `suggest_prompts` and `suggest_followups`), and increments a per-response counter in `createToolExecutionCallback`; when the count exceeds the cap it sets `followupSuggestionLimitHit` and `processStream` calls the newly threaded `stopStream` callback. run-agent-step.ts threads `stopStream: () => streamStop.abort()` (over a per-step `AbortController`) through to `processStream`.

entries.title: Agent Runtime update: run-agent-step
entries.summary: Agent Runtime changes across 3 file(s) (+371/−12).

ai.title: Agent runtime short-circuits repeated unchanged to-do lists as a no-op
ai.summary: The write_todos tool handler now compares its input against the most recently completed to-do list via `todoListKey` and `latestRecordedTodoListKey`, returning `WRITE_TODOS_UNCHANGED_MESSAGE` so a repeated list is answered as a no-op from the first repeat instead of being rewarded as a fresh success. `run-agent-step.ts` now logs an `todo_loop_recovery`/`todo_loop_stopped` metric with `fileEditToolsOffered` and, when recovery guidance is injected, builds that message from `todoLoopRecoveryMessage(agentTemplate.toolNames)` so it names the missing file-editing tools only when none is offered. The new `FILE_EDIT_TOOLS_UNAVAILABLE_NOTE` is appended by `writeTodosUnchangedMessage` and `todoLoopRecoveryMessage` only when the agent has no file-editing tool, preventing models that lack `write_file` from substituting a to-do call
ai.evidence: packages/agent-runtime/src/util/todo-loop.ts adds exports `todoListKey`, `latestRecordedTodoListKey`, `writeTodosUnchangedMessage`, `hasFileEditTool`, `FILE_EDIT_TOOLS_UNAVAILABLE_NOTE`, and `WRITE_TODOS_UNCHANGED_MESSAGE`; packages/agent-runtime/src/tools/handlers/tool/write-todos.ts now compares the incoming write_todos input via `todoListKey` against `latestRecordedTodoListKey` and returns `writeTodosUnchangedMessage` when they match; packages/agent-runtime/src/run-agent-step.ts imports `hasFileEditTool` and `todoLoopRecoveryMessage`, logs recovery/stops, and feeds `agentTemplate.toolNames` into the recovery message builder
ai.unknowns: The exact rollout cadence and which models trigger the new guidance most often are not visible in this diff

ai.title: Advertiser funnel telemetry added to analytics events
ai.summary: A new 'Web - Advertiser funnel' block of 50 enum members is added to the `AnalyticsEvent` enum in `common/src/constants/analytics-events.ts`, instrumenting the advertiser buyer journey from the /advertisers pitch through the /ads console, including landing views, expert form submissions, signups, email verification, onboarding steps, builder interactions, campaign lifecycle, top-ups, and server-side creation/approval/rejection events. The events are emitted so the funnel between the pitch page and a live campaign can be measured and drop-off diagnosed, since properties are restricted to enums, lengths, amounts, and ids (never advertiser free text, URLs, or emails per the comment referencing freebuff/web/src/components/advertisers/analytics.knowledge.md). The server-side events use the Postgres user id as distinct_id and are explicitly not billable, while top-up CREDITS events are excluded because the Stripe webhook runs in the web service and should be read from ad_spend_ledger instead.
ai.evidence: The diff adds a new 'Web - Advertiser funnel' section of 50 enum members to the `AnalyticsEvent` enum in `common/src/constants/analytics-events.ts`, inserted between `ADS_DOCK_COLLAPSED` and the 'Web - Token Count API' section, including events like `ADVERTISER_LANDING_VIEWED`, `ADVERTISER_SIGNUP_STARTED`, `ADVERTISER_BUILDER_OPENED`, `ADVERTISER_CAMPAIGN_SAVED`, `ADVERTISER_CREATED`, and `ADVERTISER_CAMPAIGN_APPROVED`, all carrying only enums, lengths, amounts, and ids (never advertiser free text, URLs, or emails).
ai.unknowns: Which services or frontend modules will emit these new advertiser funnel events and when that wiring will be enabled.
